# <a id="388d65dd82be8066afd6fcf7064b21a3" />Purpose

<a id="388d65dd82be804e9288fe78344e4ca9" />Miniprep the liquid cultures of the *recA* or CpxP plasmid-containing *E. coli*, and send the plasmids for sequencing.

# <a id="388d65dd82be80c8bb49e8a2d126a18f" />Materials & Methods

<a id="388d65dd82be809eaa5ce83ccec1d304" /><u>Materials</u>

- <a id="3a0d65dd82be80b48511c76a623a2ead" />NEB Monarch® Plasmid Miniprep Kit
- <a id="3a0d65dd82be80da88bff672e5c7bb4b" />NanoDrop 1000 Spectrophotometer
- <a id="3a0d65dd82be80f6b03ed60ff07c231c" />Plasmidsaurus Full Plasmid Sequencing

<br id="388d65dd82be80e2805de316b6132e6a" />

<a id="388d65dd82be80b0a05ac1ec7f9f0f46" />**Miniprep is based on the** [**manufacturer’s instructions**](https://www.neb.com/en-ca/protocols/monarch-plasmid-dna-miniprep-kit-protocol-t1010)**:**

1. <a id="388d65dd82be80deb353eb7d2352ca34" />200 µL RNAse buffer
2. <a id="388d65dd82be80c7a5ebc8e28a8057de" />200 µL Lysis buffer
   1. <a id="388d65dd82be809a8296c3e9d71f0e51" />invert the tube 5-6 times
   2. <a id="388d65dd82be8084b008e20b25189f11" />Wait 1 minute
3. <a id="388d65dd82be80e7bd98f169cd30039f" />400 µL Neutralization buffer
   1. <a id="388d65dd82be80e9bf3ceb126ad9da86" />invert the tube 5-6 times
   2. <a id="388d65dd82be805f8a24c787f347ed6c" />Wait 2 minutes
4. <a id="388d65dd82be80eb8c31f3d25ef783bb" />Spin at 10000 x g for 5 minutes
5. <a id="388d65dd82be801e94b9cd0e5ac2ae12" />800 µL of supernatant into the column in a collection tube
6. <a id="388d65dd82be80c0b472eaae820b0714" />Spin at 1000 x g for 5 minutes
   1. <a id="388d65dd82be80b380a7d7010de61077" />Pour the flow-through into the column again and re-spin at 1000 x g for 5 minutes
   2. <a id="388d65dd82be8031a4a8f17241504fe7" />Discard flow-through
7. <a id="388d65dd82be8040a9d9d5d3f0b03d90" />200 µL of wash 1
8. <a id="388d65dd82be808eaba6c76ee3ab28d1" />Spin at 10000 x g for 1 minute
9. <a id="388d65dd82be8025b7d3c75c100e0dd2" />400 µL of wash 2
10. <a id="388d65dd82be80378c5df9bbf7479925" />Spin at 10000 x g for 1 minute
11. <a id="388d65dd82be8042a30de2ed550a9a3c" />Discard the collection tube and place the miniprep column in a clean microcentrifuge tube
12. <a id="388d65dd82be806c985bd2e6b3cb4882" />45 µL of pre-warmed H2O
    1. <a id="388d65dd82be80c4a282f7d4df6c6a21" />incubate at room temperature for 3-4 minutes
    2. <a id="388d65dd82be800ea75cc33b358b4448" />Spin at 10000 x g for 1 minute

<br id="388d65dd82be8083a68ed586e0ae2bb5" />

<a id="388d65dd82be8015ac26dcbe5d8c46ed" />**Nanodrop-1000 Spectrophotometer**

1. <a id="388d65dd82be80e2a9bbd7c4ce685412" />Measure 2 µL of eluted plasmid using the Nanodrop-1000
2. <a id="388d65dd82be8003b5adcba129c3f9a8" />Record DNA concentration (ng/µL) and 260/280 ratio

<a id="388d65dd82be80298706e9407500fe6e" />Note: the ideal 260/280 ratio is 1.80.

<br id="388d65dd82be80a0afe2f28ae49e7924" />

<a id="388d65dd82be80a5bf24de6900b234be" />**Plasmidsaurus full-plasmid sequencing is based on Plasmidsaurus instructions:**

1. <a id="388d65dd82be805db53ee6f86c1728bb" />Add 500 ng of DNA into a PCR tube
2. <a id="388d65dd82be80199edfe0a89fa9bf84" />Top up to 15 µL total volume with H2O
3. <a id="388d65dd82be8003822ef620b7c04e0b" />Request sequencing using the Plasmidsaurus website and drop off the sample at a designated pick-up location

# <a id="388d65dd82be80f98e6be5c49af34924" />Results

<a id="388d65dd82be8063864dfcff9bd0eedf" />Miniprep yielded high concentrations of DNA for both RecA and CpxP plasmids.

- <a id="388d65dd82be80c79e57c8bd828502f5" />RecA plasmid: **99.8 ng/µL** and **260/280: 1.95**

<a id="388d65dd82be80daa0a4e5c5dbb243b0" />

<Img url="https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6279/wiki/assets/e3ad7b4a2cf85b8fa5f469082ac5a5ca.avif" alt="Example Nanodrop result for RecA plasmid. Notice the concentration, and 260/280 peak and ratio." scale={0} align="center" />

- <a id="388d65dd82be80d693ebd905e3635bc0" />CpxP plasmid: **94.1 ng/µL** and **260/280: 1.96**

<a id="388d65dd82be8009a3b6ec7653baa376" />Sequencing results yielded successfully cloned plasmids.

- <a id="388d65dd82be80fa94a8e5a9c1023e94" />*recA* plasmid: 100% matched to template DNA

<a id="3fed65dd82be80ddbb85f3964ee82272" />

- <a id="388d65dd82be803fbd52d8a3fc0cec9d" />CpxP plasmid: contained 3 point mutations (coordinates below are positions on the 2940 bp CpxP plasmid; all three were called by direct comparison against the sequence-perfect *recA* sibling plasmid)
  - <a id="388d65dd82be80498c33e78a5c01a192" />**g.2918G>A** → non-coding backbone, 23 bp upstream of the ColE1/pUC *ori* → outside the annotated origin and outside every CDS, promoter and terminator; does not matter for our application
  - <a id="388d65dd82be80358346fb8f03231164" />**c.338C>T** → silent mutation on the Cm selection gene (*cat* codon 113, TTC→TTT, p.Phe113=) → no amino-acid change, no effect
  - <a id="388d65dd82be80c0b8abdc31867e9fd5" />**c.190C>T** → missense mutation on the Cm selection gene (*cat* codon 64, GCC→GTC, **p.Ala64Val**)
    - <a id="388d65dd82be80f8bc16d19d370d75aa" />This is **Alanine → Valine**. An earlier version of this entry recorded it as Glycine → Valine; direct translation of the *cat* ORF gives Ala→Val, and there is no Gly codon at position 64.
    - <a id="dfd1e23920a745da9fb51280ac130f0d" />Residue 64 is not the His195 catalytic residue of chloramphenicol acetyltransferase, and the colonies are still able to grow on antibiotic-containing plates → the marker is functional
    - <a id="388d65dd82be8093a912d614609ce914" />The CpxP promoter and sfGFP gene are unaffected → should be fully functional!

<a id="3fed65dd82be8026a4f0ff8b12dbb5b6" />

<a id="3fed65dd82be80fcbe7dcd168c54edd2" />

# <a id="82a1d638694245d98335c78c53c5991b" />Annotated Plasmid Maps

<a id="d0cac601883147e4b36567062293de2a" />Fully annotated GenBank files for both reporters, for judges and for anyone reusing these parts. Labelled features: the ColE1/pUC *ori*, the sfGFP reporter CDS, the Shine-Dalgarno RBS, the driving promoter with its regulatory elements (the LexA/SOS operator and −35/−10 for P*recA*; the CpxR consensus box for P*cpxP*), the EcoRI cloning junction, the *cat* promoter and CmR marker, and all three terminators. The three CpxP point mutations are tagged as GenBank `variation` features carrying their coordinate, codon change and functional consequence.

<br id="46bb31c66b1c44efa65f17d0196b0ba1" />

<a id="744ede6035b84f9eb0a7e3825c85cf17" />

| <a id="b2ba5a179eca4f1b87d05e75e673c96a" />**Position** | **Change**           | **Located in**                               | **Consequence**                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <a id="93df620cd5a0415eb67431b9a47ca9b5" />2174         | C>T (*cat* c.190C>T) | CmR (*cat*) CDS, codon 64                    | Missense, GCC→GTC, p.Ala64Val. Not the catalytic His195; marker still functional |
| <a id="6c16d3045a4f4df187ef90c667667252" />2322         | C>T (*cat* c.338C>T) | CmR (*cat*) CDS, codon 113                   | Silent, TTC→TTT, p.Phe113=                                                       |
| <a id="d385a8d0eab341a1aa5fcdf13614ba09" />2918         | G>A                  | Non-coding backbone, 23 bp upstream of *ori* | None expected; outside the origin and all annotated features                     |

<br id="2267dbe2ff5e4f649a9e6cf06abaff7f" />

<a id="afcffe147fb242a19725b73c831da2da" />The reporter cassette is clean in both plasmids: the sfGFP CDS is base-for-base identical between the two constructs, and neither promoter nor any terminator carries a mutation.

<a id="caab45cbc6274fd7ba6619bb54a417f8" />Both files are plain-text GenBank. They carry a `.txt` extension because Notion does not accept `.gb`/`.gbk` uploads — rename to `.gb` to open them in SnapGene, Benchling or Geneious.

# <a id="388d65dd82be80949ff9fad5223f621a" />Summary

<a id="388d65dd82be8047a6bcd52861756704" />The cloned *recA* and CpxP plasmids are successful based on sequencing results and can be transformed into our biosensor strains (*E. coli* K-12 derivatives) for testing validation.

# <a id="388d65dd82be8003a24ef6d3ddad1dee" />Hand off/Next Steps

<a id="388d65dd82be80e384f6f85f0e06c795" />Transform the *recA* and CpxP plasmids into the biosensor strain (*E. coli* K-12 derivatives) and test the strains for validation and intended functionality.

<br id="388d65dd82be803c8446ed4152f099d8" />
